source: synthetic Scapy frames generated by `wiguard fixtures generate`
limitations: Validates detector logic, not radio-frequency realism.

scenarios.name: clean_enterprise_same_ssid
scenarios.description: Three uniform APs share one SSID (enterprise). Negative control for the environment detector.

scenarios.name: ap_restart
scenarios.description: A trusted AP reboots: TSF and sequence numbers restart once. Must not look like a twin; a sequence restart alone is weak evidence.

scenarios.name: ssid_clone_new_bssid
scenarios.description: A second AP with its own BSSID and other hardware advertises the trusted SSID. No deauthentication.

scenarios.name: classic_evil_twin
scenarios.description: SSID clone on its own BSSID while broadcast deauthentication frames forged with the real AP's BSSID push its clients away.

scenarios.name: bssid_clone_same_channel
scenarios.description: A second device copies the BSSID and beacons on the same channel with its own clock.

scenarios.name: bssid_clone_other_channel
scenarios.description: A full copy (BSSID, IEs, near-identical TSF) beacons on another channel at the same time.

scenarios.name: bssid_clone_with_deauth
scenarios.description: BSSID copy on the same channel plus a deauthentication storm.

scenarios.name: enterprise_outlier
scenarios.description: A fourth AP joins an enterprise SSID with different hardware. No trusted profiles: found by peer comparison alone.

scenarios.name: deauth_storm_only
scenarios.description: Broadcast deauthentication flood, no impersonating AP.
